# Knowledge Context Protocol (KCP)

> A structured metadata standard that makes knowledge navigable by AI agents.
> KCP is to knowledge what MCP is to tools.

KCP defines how to add a `knowledge.yaml` manifest to any project or documentation site
so AI agents can navigate it efficiently — without exploring by trial and error.
Where llms.txt gives agents a flat list, KCP gives agents a map: intents, dependency
chains, audience targeting, freshness dating, signing, and federation — all in YAML.

Validated benchmark: 53–80% fewer agent tool calls vs unguided exploration (5 frameworks).
Apache-2.0. Maintained by the Cantara Norwegian Software Development Foundation.

## Structured Navigation (for AI agents)

This repository ships a KCP v0.14 manifest, Ed25519-signed:
https://cantara.github.io/knowledge-context-protocol/knowledge.yaml

Signing public key: https://cantara.github.io/knowledge-context-protocol/.well-known/kcp-signing-key.pub

To use: fetch the manifest → parse YAML → match query against each unit's `triggers`
(keyword list) and `intent` (natural language) → fetch the `path` of the best match.
Use `relationships` to navigate related content.

Example: "How do I validate a knowledge.yaml?" → trigger `validation, schema`
→ unit `json-schema` → fetch schema/knowledge-schema.json

## KCP Toolchain

- [kcp-commands](https://github.com/Cantara/kcp-commands) — Claude Code hook, saves 33% context window
- [kcp-memory](https://github.com/Cantara/kcp-memory) — Episodic memory hub for agent networks
- [kcp-triage](https://github.com/Cantara/kcp-triage) — Automated site triage, builds KCP manifests
- [kcp-dashboard](https://github.com/Cantara/kcp-dashboard) — Terminal TUI for KCP observability

## How KCP Relates to llms.txt and MCP

- **llms.txt** — flat URL index. KCP extends this with structure, intent, and federation.
- **MCP** — connects agents to tools. KCP structures the knowledge those tools serve.
- They compose: a project can have llms.txt for breadth, knowledge.yaml for agents that understand structure.
